_id: freq rung: ism5800_24125. LICENCE-EXEMPT band pair -- 5.8 GHz (ISM 5725-5875 MHz) paired with 24.125 GHz (ISM 24.00-24.25 GHz). Both carriers move, unlike freq001-008 which only ever shift L2 inside the protected GPS L-band. MEASURED CONSEQUENCES OF THE BAND CHOICE (computed, not assumed): first-order ionospheric delay scales as 1/f^2, so this pair sees 0.0043 x the L1 ionosphere on the high carrier and 0.0738 x on the low one; the ionosphere-free combination of this pair would amplify uncorrelated code noise by 1.063 x, against 2.975 x for GPS L1/L2 -- IF amplification follows FRACTIONAL separation, and this pair is 122.5% apart against L1/L2's 22.0%. Carrier wavelengths are 12.427 mm and 51.688 mm. SPECTRUM: 150 MHz and 250 MHz of allocation respectively. HELD FIXED ON PURPOSE: codeSigma0_m stays at the golden 0.30 / 0.45 m. A higher carrier does not by itself sharpen the code -- ranging noise follows chip rate and bandwidth, not carrier frequency -- so letting it fall with band would bake in the conclusion. This run is raw dual frequency with the golden's per-tower slant-iono state, i.e. the freq002 configuration with the band moved. 24 GHz is the HIGHEST licence-exempt band that is actually usable for an Earth-space link: everything above it in unlicensed spectrum (57-71 GHz, 122-123 GHz, 244-246 GHz) sits in a molecular absorption band.
